value.quote: 2. Keep biological quantities compatible. Separate routes (oral gavage, intraperitoneal, IV), total versus unbound drug, serum versus plasma versus free brain dialysate, and bioassay versus chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats, so parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Every conversion requires a recorded justification.

value.quote: 5. Process MIC and PTA explicitly. Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators, censored categories and test method (EUCAST, CLSI or NCCLS). The EUCAST distributions were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs, and the C. albicans data are mostly truncated at 0.016 mg/L; do not read them as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize.

value.quote: 6. Produce PTA and assess feasibility. After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and IV and oral dosing scenarios to estimate the probability of target attainment (PTA) at each MIC. Process the MIC distributions and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver the PTA tables/curves, feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.
Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment.
